data.title: Fresha Capital Emerges as a Powerful Go-To Growth Engine for the Global Beauty and Wellness Professionals
data.ai_summary: Fresha Capital, its embedded financing programme with Adyen, has issued over $20 million in loans to beauty and wellness businesses since early 2026. Over 80% of borrowers returned for additional financing, with renewal amounts up 50% on average. The company is expanding into France and Spain and developing larger financing options for enterprise partners.

data.full_text:
LONDON, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fresha, the world's leading AI-powered booking platform for beauty and wellness, has reported strong performance from Fresha Capital, its embedded business financing programme developed in partnership with global financial technology platform Adyen. Since launching in early 2026, the programme has surpassed $20 million in loans issued to beauty and wellness businesses, with over 80% of borrowers returning for additional financing and renewal amounts increasing by approximately 50% on average. With more than $200 million in financing available to eligible partners, Fresha Capital is becoming an increasingly important part of the company's global financial services offering, helping businesses access the capital they need to invest, expand and manage their operations. Continue Reading

Fresha Capital The programme's performance reflects growing demand for accessible financing within the beauty and wellness industry, where businesses often face challenges securing traditional loans despite maintaining established customer bases and consistent trading activity. Out of 135,000 businesses, from single-chair to large enterprises, more than 10,000 businesses are currently eligible for financing through Fresha Capital, which is fully embedded within Fresha's all-in-one business management platform. Beauty merchants can access financing directly through their Fresha account and monitor incoming and outgoing transactions through Fresha Wallet, bringing financial services into the same system they already use to manage appointments, payments, marketing, clients and daily operations. Using advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence, Fresha Capital analyses existing business performance and payment data to help determine financing eligibility and generate pre-approved offers, removing much of the complexity traditionally associated with business lending. Eligible businesses can access financing directly through their Fresha account without lengthy applications, extensive paperwork or the need to approach a bank. Once an offer is accepted and approved, funding can be made available in seconds, giving businesses immediate access to capital when opportunities or unexpected financial pressures arise. This technology-driven approach enables Fresha to provide financing based on real trading activity, rather than relying solely on conventional, long-winded lending assessments. Fresha Capital is available across established markets including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, Sweden, Finland and the Netherlands. The company is continuing to expand its financial services offering across the European Union, most recently introducing Fresha Capital in France and Spain in September 2026. This international expansion comes as Fresha strengthens its position as the leading all-in-one software platform for the global beauty and wellness industry, extending its capabilities beyond traditional booking and business management to provide integrated financial services designed specifically for the sector.



Alongside its international expansion, Fresha is strengthening its financing capabilities to serve enterprise and multi-location beauty and wellness businesses. The company is developing financing options of up to $500,000, with longer repayment terms and greater flexibility to meet larger capital requirements. This will enable established salon groups and major brands to invest in new locations, equipment and infrastructure, positioning Fresha Capital as a powerful growth engine for the global beauty and wellness industry. Unlike traditional business lending, Fresha Capital uses advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning to analyze existing payment and business performance data, enabling financing offers tailored to the individual needs and trading activity of each business. On average, financing offered through the programme represents approximately 65% of a business's monthly takings, providing access to capital proportionate to its existing operations. Analysis of more than $20 million in financing across 1,546 providers found that inventory purchases, day-to-day cash flow support, business renovations and equipment upgrades were among the most common reasons businesses accessed capital. Renovations and premises improvements alone accounted for approximately $1.94 million, highlighting the importance of accessible funding in an industry where continued investment in physical spaces, equipment and staff is essential. The programme's impact is already evident among businesses using Fresha, including London-based barbershop SliderCuts, founded by internationally recognized barber and Fresha ambassador Mark Maciver. Known for working with high-profile clients including Stormzy, LeBron James and Anthony Joshua, Maciver faced significant financial pressure after renovation costs at his Hoxton barbershop escalated far beyond the original budget. With mounting expenses threatening the future of the business, he received a financing offer through Fresha Capital, providing the funding needed to keep SliderCuts operating. Speaking to The Times about receiving the offer, Mark Maciver, Founder of SliderCuts, said: "When that loan came through, it was like a miracle because I didn't even ask them. I was also calling them to say, 'Yo, is this real?'" Maciver's experience demonstrates the importance of accessible financing when businesses face unexpected financial pressures or opportunities for investment. Beyond immediate funding requirements, research conducted through Fresha's Capital Feedback Project found that 75% of surveyed partners with sufficient cash flow would consider accessing Fresha Capital should the need arise. Combined with the programme's strong repeat borrowing rates, these findings indicate significant potential for continued adoption as Fresha expands its financial services offering internationally. William Zeqiri, Founder and CEO of Fresha, said: "Fresha is building the most comprehensive operating system for the global beauty and wellness industry, and financial services are fundamental to that ambition. Seeing 80% of borrowers return for additional financing demonstrates the demand for this programme and the opportunity ahead of us. Through our partnership with Adyen, we're bringing sophisticated financial infrastructure directly into the hands of the businesses that need it, from independent professionals to major enterprise operators. Our ambition is to make Fresha the platform businesses turn to for everything they need to operate, invest and grow." Fresha Capital is delivered in partnership with Adyen, combining Fresha's global network of beauty and wellness businesses with Adyen's financial technology infrastructure. The collaboration reflects the growing role of embedded finance in business software, where financial products are integrated directly into the platforms businesses already rely on rather than accessed through separate banking and lending providers. By bringing financing into its wider operating platform, Fresha is creating a more connected approach to business management, combining scheduling, payments, marketing, client relationships and financial services within a single system. Dane Carmody, Head of Product at Fresha, said: "Fresha Capital was built to make business financing more accessible, using payment and performance data to provide funding that reflects how beauty and wellness businesses actually operate. The programme's strong adoption demonstrates the demand for financing that is built directly into the tools businesses already use. As we expand into new markets and develop larger financing options for enterprise partners, we're creating even more opportunities for businesses to access capital when they need it." With continued international expansion, strong repeat borrowing rates and plans to introduce larger financing options for enterprise businesses, Fresha Capital is entering its next phase of growth. The programme is becoming a central part of Fresha's global financial services strategy, reinforcing the company's ambition to build the first truly all-in-one, 360-degree operating system for the global beauty and wellness industry. About Fresha Fresha is the world's leading AI-powered booking platform for beauty and wellness, trusted by over 140,000 partner businesses across more than 120 countries. Its fully integrated ecosystem spans scheduling, payments, marketing, team management and a global consumer marketplace, giving beauty and wellness businesses everything they need to operate, grow and scale. The Fresha Marketplace connects millions of consumers with salons, spas, barbershops and wellness studios worldwide, with over one million monthly downloads and more than $1.4 billion in monthly transaction value. To learn more, visit fresha.com. Press enquiries [email protected] SOURCE Fresha

Scaling a platform creates clear opportunities to capture new market share, but growth often tests the limits of financial infrastructure. When software platforms expand into new regions or launch new product lines, managing payouts, accounts and pay-ins across fragmented providers can slow momentum. Leading software platforms are solving this by changing how they build. By consolidating financial capabilities onto a single platform, they’re removing operational friction, expanding globally and turning embedded payments into a primary growth driver. Below, learn how Fresha, Epos Now and Navan have turned complexity into a strategic advantage. Fresha launched capital across seven markets in three weeks Access to fast capital is one of the biggest operational hurdles for independent salons and beauty professionals. Fresha, a platform for the beauty and wellness industry, recognized that traditional business loans were too slow and rigid for their users. They wanted to offer tailored capital directly inside the software their customers trust, and use daily. Instead of building a capital lending program region by region, Fresha used Adyen Capital. Users received pre-approved funding offers with zero paperwork, and Fresha scaled its capital capabilities in just three weeks. Read the full Fresha story Navan scaled corporate card issuing without multiplying complexity For most business travelers, the trip ends when they get home. For finance teams, the work begins. Navan set out to make corporate travel and expense management simple by issuing physical and virtual cards directly to travelers. However, expanding card issuing globally usually requires negotiating separate banking relationships, licenses and compliance standards in every target market. By using Adyen’s global issuing capabilities on a single platform, Navan bypassed traditional bank complexity. Now, Navan can issue cards instantly, set granular spend controls and reconcile expenses in real time across markets. Read the full Navan story Epos Now evolved from a POS provider to fintech platform Setting up a POS system used to mean managing hardware sales and standard transaction fees. Epos Now wanted to offer more value to its retail and hospitality customers by adding embedded financial services. Doing that independently meant applying for banking licenses — a costly, multi-year effort — or managing multiple regional financial partners. By partnering with Adyen, Epos Now launched financial services directly within its software. They expanded into embedded payments and business accounts without becoming a bank. The result? A single integrated experience for merchants, higher customer retention and new revenue streams. data.full_text:
THESSALONIKI, Greece, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fresha, the world's leading AI-powered booking platform for beauty and wellness, is bringing some of the biggest names in international barbering to Thessaloniki this October as it returns as Mega Sponsor of HAIRFEST 2026 for the second consecutive year. Continue Reading

Fresha returns as HAIRFEST’s Mega Sponsor for the second year running. Taking place from 17–19 October at the I. Vellidis Convention Center, HAIRFEST powered by Fresha will be bigger, louder and more international than ever before, bringing together thousands of hair and barbering professionals from across Europe for three days of live shows, education and creative showcases. The stage programme will feature talent from across Europe and beyond, including Mihai Mares, Kasia Fortuna, Andrea Magri, Kristina Fedorova, Los Cut It and Stanley Liao, alongside leading Fresha ambassadors Yadiel "Arod" Rodriguez, MENSPIRE co-founder Josh Lamonaca and Gradient founder Thaddeus Jayaseelan. Arod, Jayaseelan, Lamonaca and Magri will each take to the HAIRFEST stage, bringing some of the techniques, ideas and education shaping modern barbering to a live European audience. Fresha's return comes amid major growth across its global barbering community, with active barber partners using the platform increasing 108% year on year from 2025 to 2026. Alongside that growth, Fresha has built an increasingly influential presence within the industry itself, working with leading barbers, educators, academies and businesses while investing in major barbering events around the world. From HairCon in the UK and Toronto Barbers Expo in Canada to HAIRFEST in Greece, Fresha is building a global barbering and hairdressing community that extends far beyond its technology. Its growing ambassador network brings together some of the profession's leading barbers, educators, academy founders and entrepreneurs across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Australasia. At HAIRFEST, Fresha will stand alongside some of the biggest names in professional hair and beauty, with L'Oréal Professionnel, BaBylissPRO, Moroccanoil, Schwarzkopf Professional, Panasonic and Wahl Professional among the brands supporting this year's programme. "HAIRFEST represents exactly the kind of industry environment we want Fresha to be part of," said William Zeqiri, Founder and CEO of Fresha. "Beauty and wellness has become an incredibly global community. The people shaping the industry are building audiences across borders, teaching internationally and constantly exchanging ideas with one another. Bringing some of that talent together in Thessaloniki is what makes HAIRFEST so exciting, and we're incredibly proud to return as Mega Sponsor for a second year." HAIRFEST returns for its fourth anniversary in 2026 under the theme GO BEYOND, with an international programme spanning modern barbering and hairdressing. Bringing together artists, educators, salon owners and barbers from across Europe and beyond, the event reflects an increasingly global industry where techniques, trends and education move rapidly between markets and leading professionals are building audiences far beyond their home countries. "There's a completely different energy when you're working live in front of other barbers," said Yadiel "Arod" Rodriguez, Fresha Global Ambassador. "Everyone in that room understands the craft, so you can really push what you're doing and show the thinking behind the finished result. Coming to Thessaloniki and sharing a stage with artists from different parts of the world is what makes events like HAIRFEST special. You're there to show your own work, but you're also there to watch, learn and take something away from everyone around you. I started cutting hair in my parents' garage in Puerto Rico with a clipper I bought with my lunch money. Bringing that story to a stage like HAIRFEST, in front of barbers from all over the world, means a lot to me. I'm closing Day 1, and I promise it's going to feel like a party." Education will sit at the heart of Fresha's presence throughout the weekend. Its ambassador community includes professionals working not only behind the chair, but across education, academies and business. MENSPIRE, co-founded by Josh Lamonaca, has built an international education network around modern men's hair, while Gradient founder Thaddeus Jayaseelan has built his own reputation around technical education and the development of the next generation of barbers. "Education is one of the things that keeps barbering moving forward," said Jayaseelan. "You can spend years developing your own approach, but putting yourself around other great artists immediately opens up a different way of thinking. HAIRFEST brings together people who might normally be working thousands of miles apart and gives us the chance to exchange that knowledge properly. That same sense of community is why I work so closely with Fresha. It's the only platform I use and, for me, the only one I'd want to use." That focus on international education and collaboration will run throughout this year's HAIRFEST programme, with artists from across the hair and barbering industry taking to the stage throughout the three-day event. "This year's HAIRFEST is going to be our biggest and most international yet, and having Fresha return as Mega Sponsor is a huge part of that," said George Xidaseli, CEO and Founder of HAIRFEST. "We're bringing incredible artists and educators from around the world to Thessaloniki for three days that are really about pushing the industry forward. The energy around this year's event is already building, and we can't wait to welcome everyone in October." "GO BEYOND is about raising the bar again for what people can expect from HAIRFEST," said Stefanos Polizos, Executive Director of HAIRFEST. "Across three days, we'll have live shows, education and some of the most exciting talent in hair and barbering all under one roof. Having Fresha back as Mega Sponsor allows us to make this year's event even more ambitious and create an experience that brings the international industry together here in Thessaloniki." The event marks Fresha's second consecutive year as Mega Sponsor and the latest chapter in its growing investment in global barbering. With active barber partners more than doubling year on year, an expanding international ambassador community and partnerships with some of the industry's major events, Fresha is strengthening its position at the heart of the global barbering industry. HAIRFEST powered by Fresha 2026 – GO BEYOND takes place from 17–19 October 2026 at the I. Vellidis Convention Center in Thessaloniki, Greece. data.title: Top Salon Scheduling Software Compared Features, Pricing and Costs
data.ai_summary: Eight salon scheduling platforms are compared, covering Bookeo, Mangomint, Boulevard, GlossGenius, Fresha, Vagaro, Square Appointments, and Acuity Scheduling. Pricing models vary from flat tiers to per-user fees and marketplace commissions, with tradeoffs noted for each. The comparison highlights how cost structures differ across platforms.

industries.name: Personal Care & Wellness Booking Platforms (Beauty, Fitness, Spa)

data.full_text:
Home Press Release Top Salon Scheduling Software Compared: Features, Pricing And Key Differences

Top Salon Scheduling Software Compared: Features, Pricing and Key Differences Published: 29 Sep 2026 Author: Precedence Research Share: Top Scheduling Software Compared: Head-to-Head Feature Breakdown If you run a salon or a day spa and you are shopping for scheduling software right now, the hard part is not finding options. There are dozens, and most of them will take a booking, send a reminder, and hold a card. The hard part is that the platforms are priced on completely different logic, so two systems that look almost identical on a feature grid can be several thousand dollars apart over a year, depending on how many chairs you have and where your new clients come from. This is a large and growing trade, which is part of why the software market around it is so crowded. Federal labor projections have employment of barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists growing 7 percent between 2025 and 2035, off a base of roughly 670,800 jobs. We compared eight platforms that salon and spa owners actually shortlist, and we have written every entry to the same template so the comparison is like-for-like. How This Comparison Was Put Together We started from the pages that currently rank for salon and spa scheduling queries and pulled out every vendor that appeared on more than one of them, then removed the tools that are general-purpose calendar apps with a beauty landing page attached. What was left is the eight platforms below. For each one we did the same three things. We opened the vendor's own pricing page and recorded the published numbers, including per-user charges, per-location charges and card processing rates, because those are the figures that move the annual total. We recorded the current Capterra rating and the review count, as plain text, so you can see how much evidence sits behind each score. Then we identified one limitation for every platform, including the one we placed first. We did not accept "contact us for pricing" as an answer, and no vendor paid for placement or for a particular position in the list. Ratings and prices were checked in September 2026 and they do change, so treat them as a starting point rather than a quote. The Eight Platforms At A Glance Platform Starting price Pricing model Best for Main tradeoff Capterra rating Bookeo $14.95 a month Flat tiers by staff count and booking volume Salons and spas that want a predictable bill Branches run as separate accounts 4.3 (103 reviews) Mangomint $130 a month Base fee plus per user Salons with a front desk and a full service menu High cost floor for very small teams 5.0 (344 reviews) Boulevard $140 a month per location Tiered per location Multi-location salons, spas and medspas Priced per location, entry tier caps professionals 4.6 (389 reviews) GlossGenius $24 a month Flat tiers, payments included Solo stylists and small teams Rooms, waivers and waitlist sit on higher tiers 4.8 (349 reviews) Fresha $19.95 a month Subscription plus new-client commission Salons that want marketplace demand 20 percent commission on new marketplace clients 4.8 (1,447 reviews) Vagaro $30 a month Scales with bookable calendars Mixed beauty and wellness businesses Marketing tools and branded app excluded from trial 4.7 (3,651 reviews) Square Appointments $0 a month Free tier, then per location Salons already on Square hardware No-show fees and waitlist require a paid plan 4.5 (260 reviews) Acuity Scheduling $16 a month Tiered by number of calendars Single-service providers and small studios A scheduler rather than a salon system 4.8 (5,758 reviews) 1. Bookeo Best for: salons and spas that want a predictable flat monthly bill and industry-specific scheduling rather than a percentage of every booking. If you are comparing these eight platforms on cost, this is the one where the pricing structure is the main argument. Bookeo prices on staff count and on monthly booking volume, so the bill does not move when you have a good month, and the software vendor does not take a commission out of a booking; card processing runs through Stripe, Square, or PayPal at those providers' own published rates. The appointments product is also one of three separate products (the other two are built for classes and for tours and activities), which is a different design decision from the single general-purpose system that most of this category ships. Key features Real-time booking through a widget embedded in your existing site, or a standalone branded booking page if you do not have one

Staff assigned to specific services with working hours set per staff member and per location, plus calendar sync with Google Calendar, iCal, Outlook and Office 365

Deposits, full prepayment or a card held on file, with automatic email and text reminders and online rescheduling

Client database with intake forms, prepaid packages, memberships and gift vouchers, and digital waivers as a paid add-on Pricing: five tiers, quoted on the US pricing page as Solo at $14.95, Small at $29.95, Standard at $39.95, Large at $79.95, and X-Large at $119.95 a month. The tiers run from 1 consultant and 200 bookings a month up to 60 consultants and 3,000 bookings a month. Digital waivers are an add-on at $9 to $249 a month depending on volume, and text credits are $0.09 each. The free trial is 30 days with no credit card required. Rating: 4.3 on Capterra from 103 reviews. Where it falls short: multi-branch businesses are handled through a portal in which customers search for a branch or centre and then book with that individual branch, and each branch is a standalone account that controls its own schedule, staff, customer database, sales reports and statistics. Data is not shared between branches. Each branch has its own customers, its own members and its own gift vouchers, so a voucher bought at one branch can only be redeemed at that branch. The portal manager can go into each sub-account's backend and pull portal reports (booking summaries and a revenue summary) for each sub-account, but if you are expecting one combined customer list across five sites, that is not the model. The review base is also small next to the platforms further down this list, which is worth knowing when you are reading scores. 2. Mangomint Best for: salons and spas with a front desk and a full-service menu that want one system running the floor rather than a calendar and a till kept separately. Mangomint is built on the assumption that you have a front desk and somebody standing at it. Pricing is $120 a month as a base fee plus $10 per user, so the smallest realistic monthly bill is $130, and the bill rises with headcount rather than with bookings. What you get for that is a system intended to run the whole floor rather than only the calendar, which includes point of sale, retail and inventory, forms and charting, and staff management. Key features Calendar, online booking, Express Booking and a virtual waiting room for walk-ins and gaps

Point of sale with retail and inventory, gift cards, memberships and packages

Forms and charting, client management and web chat

Staff management, reporting and multi-location support in the base plan Pricing: $120 a month base plus $10 per user, with additional locations at $120 a month each. Add-ons are priced separately, including phone at $70 a month per line, marketing from $30 a month, and payroll at $50 a month plus $8 per worker. Card processing is 2.45 percent plus 15 cents in person and 2.90 percent plus 30 cents for virtual transactions. A free trial account is available. Rating: 5.0 on Capterra from 344 reviews. Where it falls short: the cost floor. A three-stylist salon is at $150 a month before a single add-on, and a solo operator is paying for a front-desk system that will not be used. The reporting and inventory depth is real, but it is depth you have to be big enough to need. 3. Boulevard Best for: multi-location salons, spas and medspas that need per-location control, per-location reporting and treatment-side depth. Boulevard is priced and reported per location, and that is the design assumption underneath the whole product rather than an option that has been added on afterwards. The tiers escalate on the number of professionals and on the volume of texts and email blasts included. It appears on medspa shortlists about as often as it appears on salon shortlists, which is a reasonable signal about where the product depth actually sits. Key features Per-location scheduling, reporting, and staff permissions

Client messaging with included text and email allowances that scale by tier

Forms as a paid add-on for intake and consent, which matters for treatment-led businesses

Integrations including QuickBooks as a paid add-on Pricing: Essentials is $176 a month per location, or $140 with annual billing, and covers up to 5 professionals with 100 texts, 500 email blasts, and 25 GB of storage. Premier is $293, or $234 annually, and lifts that to unlimited professionals, 250 texts, and 1,000 email blasts. Prestige is $410, or $328 annually, and adds the forms add-on with 2,500 texts and 10,000 email blasts. Enterprise pricing is quoted on request. Forms is $65 a month; QuickBooks is $45 a month. Rating: 4.6 on Capterra from 389 reviews. Where it falls short: the price. Two locations on Essentials is $280 a month at least, and the entry tier stops at 5 professionals, which many two-site salons will pass quickly. Card processing rates are not published on the pricing page, so you will have to ask for them before you can compare the real cost against the platforms that do publish. 4. GlossGenius Best for: solo stylists and small teams that want one flat price with card processing included in it. Solo stylists and small teams are the audience here, and the pricing reflects that. The Standard plan is $24 a month billed annually and includes the booking site, client notifications, email and text marketing, inventory and retail, and packages and memberships, with card processing at a flat 2.6 percent. For a one-chair business, that is a straightforward number to plan against. Key features Custom booking website with unlimited client notifications

Email and text marketing included from the entry plan

Inventory, retail, packages and memberships

Forms and waivers, Google booking, automated waitlist, and room and resource management from the Gold plan Pricing: Standard is $24 a month, Gold is $48 a month, and Platinum is $148 a month, all billed annually. Medspa plans are separate at $148 and $248 a month. Card processing is a flat 2.6 percent with no extra charge for tap-to-pay or card on file; instant payouts cost 1.8 percent, and the payroll add-on is $40 a month plus $6 a seat. The free trial is 14 days with no credit card. Rating: 4.8 on Capterra from 349 reviews. Where it falls short: the features a spa needs are not on the cheap plan. Room and resource management, automated waitlist, and forms and waivers all start on Gold at $48 a month, which is double the headline price. If you are a hair salon, the Standard plan may well be enough; if you have treatment rooms, it probably is not. 5. Fresha Best for: salons that want marketplace demand and are willing to pay a commission for the new clients that marketplace sends them. With Fresha, the subscription price is not the figure that decides what you pay in a year. Fresha charges $19.95 a month for an independent professional and $14.95 per team member per month for a team, which is genuinely low, and it then takes a 20 percent one-time commission on every new client who books through the Fresha marketplace, with a minimum fee of $6 per client, while returning clients are free. That commission is a customer acquisition channel with a price attached to it, and our view is that it gets misread as free software more often than any other pricing arrangement in this category. Key features Marketplace exposure to consumers searching for salons in your area

Subscription priced per team member rather than per location

Card processing built in, with buy now pay later available through Klarna

Optional add-ons for loyalty, insights, review generation, and an AI concierge Pricing: Independent is $19.95 a month, Team is $14.95 per team member a month, and enterprise pricing is quoted on request. The new-client marketplace commission is 20 percent with a $6 minimum per client. Online card payments are 2.79 percent plus $0.20; in-person payments are 2.29 percent plus $0.20 with an extra 10 cents for tap-to-pay, and manual card entry is 3.30 percent plus $0.20. Add-ons include client loyalty at $59.95 a month per location, insights at $9.95 per bookable team member, and an AI concierge at $99.95 a month per location. Rating: 4.8 on Capterra from 1,447 reviews. Where it falls short: the commission is charged on new clients, which means the cost of the platform rises exactly when the business is growing. If most of your new bookings already come from your own site, your own social accounts or word of mouth, you are paying a marketplace rate for demand you generated yourself, and you should model that before you switch. 6. Vagaro Best for: mixed beauty and wellness businesses where several different kinds of providers share one roof and one booking system. Vagaro has been in this market a long time, and it shows in the breadth of the feature list and in the size of the review base, which is over 3,600 on Capterra. The entry price is low and the platform scales by the number of bookable calendars rather than by location, which suits mixed businesses where hair, nails, massage and fitness share a roof. Key features Booking, calendars and client records for beauty, wellness and fitness businesses in one system

Website builder, marketing tools and a branded client app available in the subscription

Merchant services with a card reader included on sign-up

Pricing tiers selected by the number of bookable calendars, from one up to seven or more Pricing: the published rate is $23.99 a month as an introductory price for the first six months, with a standard price of $30.00, and the plan cost rises as you add bookable calendars. The free trial is 30 days and covers all features except email marketing, text marketing and the branded app. Card processing rates are quoted through Vagaro merchant services rather than published on the pricing page. Rating: 4.7 on Capterra from 3,651 reviews. Where it falls short: the trial excludes email marketing, text marketing and the branded app, which are three of the things a salon is most likely to be evaluating. You can trial the calendar but not the growth tools, so the first real test of those happens after you are already paying. 7. Square Appointments Best for: salons that already take payment on Square hardware and want the booking calendar attached to the till. There is a free tier here, and for a solo stylist who already takes payments on Square hardware it is a reasonable place to start, because booking is attached to the till and the reporting is one system rather than two. The paid tiers are priced per location and they also buy down the card processing rate, which is unusual and worth doing the arithmetic on if your card volume is high. Key features Online booking site, integrations, appointment reminders and unlimited staff calendars on the free plan

Cancellation policy, no-show fees, multi-staff appointment booking and a waitlist on the Plus plan

Future bookings report, service cost tracking and resource management on the Premium plan

Booking, payments, and reporting in one account with Square point of sale Pricing: Square Free is $0 a month, Square Plus is $49 a month per location, and Square Premium is $149 a month per location. In-person card processing is 2.6 percent plus 15 cents on Free, 2.5 percent plus 15 cents on Plus, and 2.4 percent plus 15 cents on Premium. Online payments are 3.3 percent plus 30 cents on Free and 2.9 percent plus 30 cents on the paid plans. Paid plans include a trial period. Rating: 4.5 on Capterra from 260 reviews. Where it falls short: the free plan is thin in the places where salons actually lose money. Cancellation policies, no-show fees, and the waitlist all require Plus at $49 a month per location. Payment processing is also Square-only, so if you have a processing rate you like elsewhere, you cannot bring it with you. 8. Acuity Scheduling Best for: single-service providers, mobile therapists, and small studios that need a scheduler rather than a salon management system. Acuity Scheduling is a scheduling tool that a lot of beauty professionals use, rather than a salon management system that happens to schedule. It is owned by Squarespace; the calendar and intake side is well built, and it is priced by the number of calendars you need rather than by staff or by location. For a single-service provider, a small studio or a mobile therapist, that is often the right shape. Key features Client self-scheduling with unlimited services and appointments on every plan

Payments through Stripe, Square, PayPal, and Venmo

SMS reminders, packages, and gift certificates from the Standard plan

HIPAA business associate agreement and custom API and CSS access on Premium Pricing: Starter is $16 a month billed annually or $20 monthly and includes 1 calendar. Standard is $27 annually or $34 monthly and includes up to 6 calendars. Premium is $49 annually or $61 monthly and includes up to 36 calendars. The free trial is 7 days and does not require a credit card. Rating: 4.8 on Capterra from 5,758 reviews. Where it falls short: it is a scheduler, and the salon-specific layer is not the centre of the product. There is no retail-first design, and the trial is only 7 days, which is short if you intend to import a client list, build a service menu, and test a real week of bookings before you decide. What to compare besides the booking calendar Most feature grids in this category compare the same eight things, and most of those eight are now table stakes. These are the areas where the platforms above genuinely differ. Online booking and per-staff calendars Every platform here will publish availability and take a booking. What varies is whether the system understands that a service is tied to a specific person with specific hours, that some services can only be performed by some staff, and that two stylists cannot occupy the same station. If you have more than two people, ask to see double-booking prevention configured, not described. Deposits, Cancellation Windows and No-Show Fees This is the group of settings that has money directly attached to it, and it is the group where the detail is worth checking carefully. A workable configuration will let you require a deposit or full prepayment on selected services, hold a card on file for the rest, define a cancellation window, and then charge the fee automatically when somebody cancels inside that window. Note that once you store a card to charge a late-cancellation fee later, you are handling payment account data. The standards for that are set by the card industry's security council, which was founded in 2006 by the major payment brands, and compliance is a question you should be asking your software vendor rather than assuming. Client Self-Service: Rescheduling, Cancelling And The Waitlist Self-service is the feature that removes phone calls, and it has two halves. The first is that a client can move or cancel a booking from the confirmation email or a client area without calling the salon. The second is that when a slot is released, the system automatically offers it to a waitlist rather than leaving a hole in the day. Plenty of platforms do the first. Fewer do the second, and on some of them the automated waitlist sits on a higher tier, so check which plan it is on before you price the system. Memberships, Packages And Gift Vouchers If you sell a six-session package or a monthly membership, the software has to track the balance, the expiry and the recurring charge, and it has to do that at the point of booking rather than in a spreadsheet afterwards. Gift vouchers are a separate question again, particularly for multi-site businesses, because the rules about where a voucher can be redeemed differ by platform. The Layer Beyond Booking: Point Of Sale, Retail And Staff Commission For a hair salon with a retail shelf and a commission structure, the booking calendar is maybe half the job. Point of sale, inventory, and commission tracking on both services and product sales are the parts that decide whether you are running one system or three. Mangomint and Boulevard are built with that layer in mind; the lower-priced schedulers generally are not, and that is a fair reason for the price gap. Client Apps And Staff Apps These are two different things, and they get conflated. A client app is a booking app your customers install, and it is mostly a retention and rebooking tool. A staff app is what your team uses to see their own schedule, check a client note before a service, and take a payment on the floor. Some vendors charge for one or the other, and a branded client app is frequently an add-on rather than an inclusion. Integrations The list to check is short and specific: your calendar (Google, Outlook, iCal or Office 365), your payment processor, your accounting package, and your email marketing tool. If a platform forces its own payment processing, that is not automatically bad, but it does mean the card rate is part of the subscription decision rather than separate from it. The Pricing Model, Which Is Where Most Of The Money Is Three models are in use across the eight platforms above, and they behave very differently as a business grows. A flat tier priced on staff count and booking volume is predictable, and it does not cost you more in a month when trade is good. The second model, a base fee plus a per-user charge, is manageable at three people and gets expensive at twelve, because the per-user line is charged whether or not that person is generating bookings. The third model, a commission on new clients, is inexpensive while you are quiet and increasingly expensive while you are growing, which is the opposite of what most owners assume when they sign up. Salons are small businesses in the statistical sense as well as the everyday one, since by the federal government's own count 99.9 percent of businesses are small, and at that scale a $10 per-user line item is not a rounding error. Build the twelve-month total under each model with your real numbers before you compare feature lists. Solo, Single-Site Or Multi-Location Changes The Answer For a solo stylist or a single mobile therapist, the calendar is the product, and almost everything else is overhead. GlossGenius, Acuity Scheduling, and the free Square Appointments tier all make sense at that size, and paying $130 a month for inventory and payroll you do not use is a poor trade. For a single location with three to ten staff, the decision usually comes down to whether you need the retail and commission layer. If you do, Mangomint and Boulevard are the serious candidates and the cost is justified. If you do not, a flat-tier platform such as Bookeo or a per-calendar platform such as Vagaro will cover the same booking workload for a fraction of the monthly cost. For multi-location businesses, ask one blunt question early: what exactly is shared between sites, and what is not. Some platforms give you one account with several locations inside it and consolidated reporting. Others, including Bookeo with its portal model, run each branch as a separate account with its own customers, staff, reports and vouchers, and give the portal manager access to each sub-account plus per-sub-account portal reports rather than a merged view. Neither approach is wrong. A franchise where each branch is independently owned often prefers the separated model, while a three-site group under one owner usually wants the consolidated one. What causes trouble is buying the first when you assumed the second, so get the vendor to demonstrate it on your own structure before you sign anything. Which One To Pick Naming one overall winner here would be tidy, and it would also be wrong, because the eight platforms are aimed at businesses of quite different sizes. Mangomint and Boulevard are the strongest choices when the business is large enough to need the full operations layer and can carry the monthly cost of it. For solo operators and very small teams, GlossGenius, Acuity Scheduling and the free Square Appointments tier are all sensible starting points. Fresha is a good arrangement if the marketplace is genuinely bringing you clients you would not otherwise have had, and a poor one if it is not, so that is the number to check first. Vagaro sits in the middle and tends to suit mixed beauty and wellness businesses that have several kinds of providers under one roof. If what you want is salon scheduling software with a predictable flat monthly cost, industry-specific booking rather than a general calendar tool, and no commission taken out of your bookings, Bookeo is built for that buyer, with the caveat about branch separation noted above. Whichever way you go, work out the twelve-month total under each pricing model using your own staff count and your own new-client numbers before you compare anything else. The feature lists across these eight platforms are fairly similar to one another. The annual invoices are not.

#London #United Kingdom #Fresha #grooming #Barbering Fresha Becomes Leading Software for the Global Barbering Sector Fresha Takes the Lead in the Barbering Software Industry



Fresha has solidified its position as the leading software provider for barber businesses around the world, primarily due to its AI-powered booking platform. The company's surge is characterized by a 108% increase in active barber partners year-on-year, showcasing Fresha's satisfaction among barbers globally. Their community includes independent barbers and well-recognized franchises alike, spanning countries like the UK, US, Canada, Australia, and various parts of Europe.



A Growing Barbering Community

Fresha's clientele reflects the dynamic nature of the barbering industry. The platform serves a range of barber professionals—from solo entrepreneurs to well-known franchises such as MENSPIRE, Rascals, Ted's Grooming Room, Gould Barbers, and Blackbox. The diverse ambassador network, comprising top barbers and educators from various regions, symbolizes this growing international community. Recently, influential figures like Cal Newsome and Sheldon Edwards have joined this network, enhancing its eclectic mix of professionals.



Events and Partnerships

Beyond the technical services, Fresha is deeply entrenched in the barbering community through various partnerships and events. The brand supports more than 25 significant events aimed at promoting professional hair and self-care, including a five-year collaboration with HairCon in the UK and a multi-year agreement with HAIRFEST. Its influence has extended across North America with major gatherings in Toronto and other U.S. cities, reflecting its deepening roots internationally.



Evolution of the Barbering Industry

Today's barbering landscape is characterized by a wave of ambition and entrepreneurial spirit. Independent barbers are establishing strong personal brands, while established shops expand into multiple locations. Many of the leading figures in the industry are now creating academies, educational businesses, and their own product lines. Fresha is evolving alongside these trends, offering tools that cater to the complexities of managing bookings, payments, and marketing, all from a single platform.



Technological Advancements

The introduction of AI-powered features like the AI Concierge has revolutionized how barbers manage client communications. This innovation allows barber businesses to handle client inquiries, appointment bookings, and rescheduling seamlessly while they focus on their craft. The platform also includes features like Professional Profiles and a Smart Website Builder, which empowers barbers to enhance their online presence and grow their clientele.



William Zeqiri, Founder and CEO of Fresha, states, “We want Fresha to furnish barbers with the tools to create lasting businesses—whether that means running a single chair exceptionally well or establishing a multi-location empire.” This pragmatic approach to technology, inspired by actual barber experiences, fuels Fresha’s growth trajectory.



The Future of Barbering

The barbering field is transforming significantly, with changing aspirations for newer generations where merely mastering skills isn’t sufficient. It’s a space where barbers form teams, open new locations, foster international education, and create global brands. As the industry's ambitions increase, robust back-end systems become crucial for these developments.



Fresha continues to adapt its service model, focusing on the requirements of the barbering community it aims to support. From independent professionals to larger brands expanding their reach, Fresha’s commitment to empowering the barbering industry is evident through its ongoing investments in technology, partnership networks, and community-building initiatives for the evolving sector.



About Fresha

Fresha is the world's foremost AI-driven booking platform for beauty and wellness, helping over 140,000 partner businesses operate efficiently across more than 120 countries. The all-inclusive ecosystem includes scheduling, payment processing, marketing, team management, and global marketplace connectivity, thus providing vital support to beauty and wellness enterprises. data.full_text:
LONDON, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fresha, the world's leading AI-powered booking platform for beauty and wellness, is now the leading software powering barber businesses globally, backed by 108% year-on-year growth in active barber partners and a rapidly expanding barbering community across major markets including the United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Australia and Europe. Fresha's leadership extends beyond its technology, with some of the industry's most influential barbers, educators and entrepreneurs representing the platform internationally, alongside long-term partnerships with major barbering events and communities around the world. Continue Reading

HairFest, powered by Fresha Fresha's growing barbering community spans independent professionals and barbershops through to some of the industry's most recognized franchises, including MENSPIRE, Rascals, Ted's Grooming Room, Gould Barbers, and Blackbox. Its global ambassador network reflects the increasingly international nature of the profession, bringing together leading barbers and educators from the UK, Europe and North America, including Josh Lamonaca, Sam Bentham, Thaddeus Jayaseelan, Andrea Amighetti, Alexi Michael and US-based Yadiel "A-Rod" Rodriguez. The network continues to expand, with barber and educator Cal Newsome and Sheldon Edwards, educator and owner of HD CUTZ, among the latest industry names to join Fresha as global ambassadors. Beyond the platform, Fresha now supports a global calendar of more than 25 trailblazing professional hair and selfcare events and activations. This includes a landmark five-year partnership with HairCon Powered by Fresha in the UK, a multi-year exclusive global partnership with HAIRFEST, and an expanding presence across North America, where Fresha has brought its barbering community together through major industry moments in Toronto and continues to deepen its presence across the United States. Fresha's wider barbering footprint now stretches from London and Manchester to Toronto and the US, as well as Australia, Bali, Romania and beyond. That international momentum reflects a barbering industry that is becoming increasingly ambitious, entrepreneurial and commercially sophisticated. Across established barbering markets such as the UK and fast-growing communities across North America, independent barbers are building powerful personal brands, established shops are expanding into multiple locations, and some of the profession's biggest names are developing academies, education businesses, products and international communities alongside their work behind the chair. Fresha has grown with that ambition, giving businesses the infrastructure to manage bookings, payments, clients, teams, commissions, marketing, reporting and online discovery from one connected platform, while continuing to introduce AI-powered technology designed to take more of the operational workload away from professionals. For barbers, where the person delivering the service is often also responsible for managing and growing the business, that technology has a particularly important role to play. Fresha allows independent professionals to manage their entire operation from one place, while giving larger barbershops and multi-location groups the controls and visibility required to manage increasingly complex businesses. Newer capabilities, including AI Concierge, can answer client calls while barbers are busy behind the chair, helping clients book, reschedule and manage appointments using live information from the business. Professional Profiles, Online Reputation and Smart Website Builder give barbers powerful ways to showcase their work, build their reputation and grow their presence beyond the shop itself. "Barbering is one of the most entrepreneurial communities within the global selfcare industry, and the growth we're seeing reflects just how quickly these businesses are evolving," said William Zeqiri, Founder and CEO of Fresha. "We want Fresha to give barbers the infrastructure to build serious, enduring businesses, whether that means running one chair exceptionally well, growing a team, opening multiple locations or building an international brand. Seeing our active barber partners more than double in a year is incredibly exciting, but for us this is only the beginning. We intend to keep investing in the technology, people and communities pushing barbering forward." "Barbering has changed enormously, and the opportunity for the next generation is so much bigger than simply becoming great behind the chair," said Josh Lamonaca, Co-founder of MENSPIRE Salon and MENSPIRE Academy and Head of Hair Education at Fresha. "Barbers are building teams, opening locations, educating internationally and creating brands with global audiences. As those ambitions grow, the systems behind the business become incredibly important. What excites me about Fresha is that it isn't looking at barbering from the outside. It is listening to the people within it and building technology that can grow alongside where we want to take this industry." The rapid growth of Fresha's barbering community reflects a wider ambition to become more than the software used behind the chair. From its established barbering community across the UK and Europe to its expanding presence throughout the United States and wider North American market, Fresha is investing in the technology, people and communities shaping the profession at a global level. From independent professionals building loyal local client bases to established brands expanding teams, locations and academies internationally, Fresha is building the infrastructure to support a barbering industry that is becoming more ambitious, connected and influential around the world. About Fresha Fresha is the world's leading AI-powered booking platform for beauty and wellness, trusted by over 140,000 partner businesses across more than 120 countries. Its fully integrated ecosystem spans scheduling, payments, marketing, team management and a global consumer marketplace, giving beauty and wellness businesses everything they need to operate, grow and scale. The Fresha Marketplace connects millions of consumers with salons, spas, barbershops and wellness studios worldwide, with over one million monthly downloads and more than $1.4 billion in monthly transaction value. To learn more, visit fresha.com. Press enquiries press@fresha.com SOURCE Fresha

ⓘ This article is third-party content and does not represent the views of this site. We make no guarantees regarding its accuracy or completeness.

Mona Kattan has built a global brand around beauty, fragrance, and selfcare.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260910087376/en/

Beauty Mogul & Founder of KAYALI, Mona Kattan

As the founder of KAYALI Fragrances, one of the world’s most influential luxury fragrance brands, Mona has spent years helping shape consumer beauty trends while inspiring millions through her passion for wellness, confidence, and personal expression. Her recommendations are trusted by beauty enthusiasts around the world, making her one of the industry’s most recognized voices. That’s why the platform she uses to discover and book beauty and wellness appointments matters, and for Mona Kattan, that platform is Fresha, the world’s leading beauty and wellness booking platform.

For Mona, the appeal extends far beyond convenience alone. As a global entrepreneur who regularly travels between Dubai, London, New York, Los Angeles, and international beauty events, discovering exceptional beauty and wellness businesses has become an important part of her lifestyle.

Whether she’s searching for a trusted facialist before a major launch, booking a wellness treatment while travelling, finding a highly rated hair specialist in a new city, or exploring the latest self-care experiences, Mona values platforms that make discovery simple, transparent, and trustworthy.

That is where Fresha stands apart.

The platform is home to one of the beauty and wellness industry’s largest and most extensive marketplaces, bringing together premium salons, spas, clinics, medspas, barbershops, fitness studios, and wellness destinations in a single destination. Whether booking a haircut, colour appointment, facial, massage, laser treatment, injectables consultation, manicure, wellness experience, or fitness class, consumers can discover and compare thousands of businesses, browse imagery, read reviews, and book with confidence.

Whether returning to a trusted favourite or searching for somewhere entirely new, Fresha gives consumers everything they need to make informed decisions within a seamless booking experience. For beauty enthusiasts like Mona, discovery is often just as important as the appointment itself.

Rather than relying solely on recommendations or endless online searches, Fresha allows consumers to explore highly rated businesses, uncover new experiences, and find trusted professionals wherever they are in the world. With verified reviews, transparent pricing, real-time availability, and instant booking, the platform has become a trusted companion for consumers looking to get more from their beauty and wellness journey.

“I’m always looking for incredible beauty and wellness experiences, especially when I’m travelling,” said Mona Kattan, Founder & CEO of KAYALI. “What I love about Fresha is that it combines discovery and convenience in one place. You can browse reviews, explore different businesses, compare options, and book instantly. It gives you confidence that you’re finding the best experiences wherever you are. Fresha is the most popular booking app for beauty and wellness in the world.”

For William Zeqiri, Founder and CEO of Fresha, Mona’s use of the platform reflects a broader evolution in how consumers discover beauty and wellness services.

“Beauty consumers have more choice than ever before,” said Zeqiri. “People aren’t simply booking the closest salon anymore. They’re researching, comparing reviews, exploring services, and actively seeking out the very best experiences. That’s exactly what Fresha was built for. We want to help consumers discover incredible beauty and wellness businesses while helping those businesses reach more clients than ever before.”

Fresha Achieves NF525 Certification, Reinforcing Its Commitment to France's Beauty and Selfcare Industry
Fresha Achieves NF525 Certification, Reinforcing Its Commitment to France's Beauty and Selfcare Industry
PARIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Fresha, the world’s leading beauty and wellness booking platform, has achieved NF525 certification for its Point of Sale (POS) software. This important milestone strengthens Fresha’s offering in France and enables more beauty, wellness and selfcare businesses across the country to use the platform.
“France is an incredibly important market for Fresha, and achieving NF525 certification is a major step forward in what we can offer businesses here," says Baptiste Donnedieu, General Manager of France at Fresha.
Share
France is one of Fresha’s fastest-growing markets. Achieving NF525 certification reflects the company’s commitment to meeting the needs of French businesses and making its platform accessible to partners of all sizes, from independent professionals and single-location salons to clinics, spas and enterprise companies.
NF525 is an independent certification issued by AFNOR Certification, with the certification process managed by INFOCERT. This certification confirms that Fresha’s POS software complies with French anti-fraud regulations introduced under Law No. 2015-1785. These rules are designed to ensure that transaction records are securely stored and cannot be altered or deleted without a record.
Dane Carmody, Head of Product at Fresha, who led the certification project, said: “Achieving NF525 certification was an important undertaking for our team and required us to meet a rigorous set of requirements. Throughout the project, our focus was on making sure Fresha met the needs of the French market while remaining simple and intuitive for our partners to use. We’re proud to have reached this milestone. French businesses can now use Fresha’s POS software with the added confidence that the way their transaction records are stored and protected has been independently assessed.”
Baptiste Donnedieu, General Manager of France at Fresha, said: “France is an incredibly important market for Fresha, and achieving NF525 certification is a major step forward in what we can offer businesses here. We are not simply bringing a global platform to France; we are continuing to develop Fresha around the specific needs of the French market. This certification gives our partners greater confidence in how their transaction records are managed. It also means that more businesses across France can use Fresha to manage their bookings, clients, payments and daily operations in one connected place, whether they are an ambitious independent or a larger business with multiple locations.”
With its NF525-certified POS software, Fresha partners in France can manage sales alongside bookings, payments, client relationships, marketing and reporting through one platform. This makes everyday operations simpler while giving businesses confidence that their transaction records meet French requirements.
Fresha’s NF525 certification will continue to be reviewed through regular checks by INFOCERT, including an annual audit. This provides partners with ongoing independent assurance as Fresha continues to invest in its product, team and presence in France.

data.author: Fashionnetwork.Com Ww

industries.name: Face Makeup (Foundation, Concealer, Powder, Blush, Bronzer, Highlighter)

data.full_text:
Searches for over-40s beauty rise as does older consumers' confidence - Fresha report By



Nigel TAYLOR Published

September 4, 2026 Women over 40 are increasingly seeking beauty advice designed specifically for them, with new Google search data revealing huge year-on-year increases across skincare, make-up and beauty searches.





AFP

Searches for ‘over 40 beauty’ have rocketed 525% over the past year, while searches for 'women over 40 make-up' have risen 396%, according to AI-powered booking platform Fresha.



The findings “point to a growing appetite for beauty advice that acknowledges how skin changes with age, rather than treating younger skin as the default,” it said. Also, searches for ‘skincare over 40’ have surged 391% over the past year, reaching around 4,000 searches in the past month.



Meanwhile, the much broader term ‘mature skin make-up’ is up 73% year-on-year and attracted around 43,000 searches in the past month, “suggesting this is moving well beyond a niche beauty conversation”.



Fresha beauty expert Danielle Louise said the search increases “reflect a beauty consumer who wants more relevant advice, rather than being told she needs to look younger.



“For a long time, so much beauty advice has been built around the idea that ageing is something women should try to hide. What we're seeing now feels much more practical. Women want to understand what works for their skin now, rather than necessarily trying to recreate how their skin looked at 25.”



She added: “With make-up, I think we're seeing the same thing. People aren't necessarily searching because they want to look younger. They want to know how to make their make-up sit well, how to work with texture and how to choose products and techniques that suit their skin as it is today.”

data.title: Fresha steps up global expansion with Mexico & Germany hires
data.ai_summary: Fresha appointed Carlos Walther as head of commercial for Mexico and Mazen Tadli as general manager of Germany, opening a Berlin office. data.full_text:
Fresha, the London-based AI-powered marketplace and business management platform for the beauty and wellness industry, has announced senior hires in Mexico and Germany as part of its global expansion.

Founded in 2015 by William Zeqiri and Nick Miller – who were included in BusinessCloud’s Founder 250 list – Fresha is one of the fastest-growing beauty and wellness platforms in the world.

In May, the firm secured a £60m ($80m) primary growth investment from funds managed by KKR, valuing the company at more than $1bn.

Fresha has appointed Carlos Walther as head of commercial for Mexico.

Working closely with Scott O’Brien, general manager of North America, Walther will drive Fresha’s expansion in Mexico.

He will focus on growing Fresha’s market presence, acquiring and supporting new partners, developing strategic relationships and helping beauty and wellness businesses grow through its integrated booking, payments, marketplace and business management platform.

The Mexico office will also act as a launchpad for further expansion across Latin America, with Fresha planning additional offices or bases in Brazil, Argentina and beyond.

William Zeqiri, founder and CEO of Fresha, commented: “As Fresha continues its global expansion, Mexico represents one of our most dynamic and highest-potential growth markets.

“The country’s beauty and wellness sector is thriving, and businesses are actively seeking modern, integrated technology to transform their operations. With Carlos Walther leading our commercial team on the ground alongside our North American leadership, we’re excited to deepen our commitment to Mexico and help local businesses unlock their full growth potential.”

Walther said: “I’m excited to build Fresha’s commercial presence in Mexico from the ground up and work closely with local businesses as we grow.”

Fresha has also appointed Mazen Tadli as general manager of Germany and opened a new office in the heart of Berlin.

The office will serve as Fresha’s regional base for scaling its commercial operations and strengthening its presence across Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

The move forms part of Fresha’s wider global expansion, which includes establishing headquarters across Southern Europe, Northern Europe and France.

Fresha Appoints Mazen Tadli as General Manager for the DACH Region to Drive Growth Across Germany, Austria and Switzerland Fresha, the world’s most recommended AI-powered booking platform for beauty and wellness, is accelerating its expansion across the DACH region with the appointment of Mazen Tadli as General Manager of Germany, alongside the opening of Fresha’s brand-new office located in the heart of Berlin. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260827179291/en/ Mazen Tadli, General Manager of Germany and the DACH region at Fresha The new office will serve as Fresha’s regional base for scaling its commercial operations and strengthening its presence across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, some of Europe’s most important beauty, wellness and selfcare markets. This move comes alongside Fresha’s major global expansion, which includes establishing headquarters across Southern Europe, Northern Europe, and France. Working closely with Fresha’s global leadership team, Tadli will focus on growing the local team, building relationships with businesses and industry partners, and helping more selfcare businesses benefit from Fresha’s integrated booking, payments, marketplace and business management platform. The appointment marks a new phase of dedicated, locally led growth for Fresha in the region. By combining experienced regional leadership with Fresha’s global infrastructure, the company aims to deliver an experience tailored to the needs of DACH businesses, from independent professionals and owner-operated studios to multi-location groups and enterprise brands. Mazen Tadli, General Manager of Germany at Fresha, commented: “Germany, Austria and Switzerland have highly developed beauty and wellness industries, with ambitious businesses looking for technology that can support both their day-to-day operations and their long-term growth. Fresha has a significant opportunity to bring these businesses a fully connected platform that makes it easier to manage their operations, reach new clients and deliver exceptional customer experiences.” “My priority is to build a strong local presence and work closely with businesses across the region. By listening to our partners and combining that local understanding with Fresha’s global technology and marketplace, we can deliver meaningful value for businesses of every size. I’m excited to lead Fresha’s next chapter in DACH and build the team, partnerships and market presence needed to establish Fresha as the platform of choice for the region’s beauty and wellness industry.” Tadli brings more than 12 years of experience in technology, business development and commercial leadership, with particular expertise in scaling digital platforms across the food and hospitality sectors. Before joining Fresha, he spent more than six years at restaurant technology company Flipdish, initially serving as Country Manager for DACH before becoming General Manager for DACH and France. In these roles, he led regional market development and helped independent hospitality businesses adopt technology designed to strengthen their operations and digital sales. Earlier in his career, Tadli served as Head of Business Development at bloomon, where he led growth initiatives in Germany and managed the infrastructure and teams supporting the company’s expansion. He also held several leadership positions at foodora, including Head of Key Account Management for Germany, building and managing commercial teams in Hamburg and across the wider German market. His appointment brings extensive experience in market entry, B2B growth and the development of high-performing local teams to Fresha’s global organization. William Zeqiri, Founder and CEO of Fresha, commented: “As Fresha rapidly scales across the globe, we’re placing experienced commercial leaders in strategic markets where we can expand our presence and help local businesses grow. Fresha has always been built with a global-first approach, and with Mazen leading DACH, we’re excited to accelerate our growth across Germany, Austria, Switzerland and the rest of Europe. We’re also opening 100 new sales positions in Germany to support this next phase of growth.” The DACH region now enters a new phase of locally led expansion within Fresha’s global network. With dedicated regional leadership based in Berlin, Fresha will work to help businesses across Germany, Austria and Switzerland simplify their operations, connect with more clients and unlock new opportunities for growth. About Fresha Fresha is the world's leading AI-powered booking platform for beauty and wellness, trusted by over 140,000 partner businesses across more than 120 countries. Its fully integrated ecosystem spans scheduling, payments, marketing, team management, and a global consumer marketplace, giving beauty and wellness businesses everything they need to operate, grow, and scale. The Fresha Marketplace connects millions of consumers with salons, spas, barbershops, and wellness studios worldwide, with over one million monthly downloads and more than $1.4 billion in monthly transaction value. To learn more, visit fresha.com. Media contact

data.full_text:
Turborepo vs Nx vs Lerna: 7x CI Speed Gap [2026]

Elias Virtanen August 23, 2026 21 min read

Monorepos stopped being a niche choice years ago, and by August 2026 the fight over which tool orchestrates that monorepo has narrowed to three real contenders: Turborepo, Nx, and Lerna. Every JavaScript and TypeScript team running more than two or three packages in one repository eventually asks the same question: does the caching engine actually save CI money, or is it marketing? This comparison pulls version numbers, GitHub star counts, npm download figures, pricing tables, and independent benchmark data to answer that question with numbers instead of vibes.

The short version: Turborepo’s turbo package sits in the 2.10.x line as of early August 2026 (v2.10.8 published August 5), Nx just shipped its v23 major release on June 16 with 23.1 following in August, and Lerna — now stewarded by the Nx team since 2022 — has moved to a v10.0.x line as of late July 2026. None of the three is dead. All three ship active releases. But they solve different-sized problems, and picking the wrong one costs real engineering hours during CI waits.

Industry insights, the latest tech news, and special interviews, all in the Tech Insider Newsletter. One email a week. No spam, unsubscribe anytime.
